respuestas.negativa: I can only help with growing plants. I don't give information about doses, consumption or sales.
respuestas.amarillas: Yellow leaves usually point to over- or under-watering, nitrogen deficiency or light stress. Check watering and the distance to the lamp first. If it keeps getting worse, ask a specialist.
respuestas.plagas: Check the underside of the leaves and isolate the affected plant while you investigate. If the infestation spreads, a specialist can recommend the right treatment.
respuestas.diagnostico: To diagnose, sort the clues: are the affected leaves new or old? Is the problem even or in spots? How are watering, pH and light? Rule out the simplest causes first (watering, light, pH) before thinking of deficiencies or pests, and change one thing at a time so you know what worked.
respuestas.nutrientes: Nutrients are split into macronutrients (N, P, K, calcium, magnesium and sulfur) and micronutrients (iron, boron, zinc, etc.). Mobile ones (N, P, K and Mg) show first on old leaves; less mobile ones (Ca, Fe and B), on new leaves. Before fertilizing, check watering, light and pH: many "deficiencies" are actually pH or watering problems.
respuestas.inerte: In inert substrates the medium gives no nutrients, so watering with nutrient solution is key. Water often with moderate volumes and allow some drainage to avoid salt buildup.
respuestas.hidro: In hydroponics, measure the solution's pH and EC regularly (pH usually stays between 5.5 and 6.5), adjust to the stage and renew the solution so it doesn't run out or get too concentrated. If the pump or aeration fails, act fast: roots get damaged within hours.
respuestas.dli: DLI is the total light a plant gets in a day: PPFD × hours of light × 3600 ÷ 1,000,000. For example, 300 µmol/m²/s for 16 hours gives about 17 mol/m²/day. As a reference, leafy greens usually need 12 to 17 and fruiting crops 20 to 30.
respuestas.germinacion: Sow at a depth of 2 to 3 times the seed's diameter and keep the medium moist but not soaked. Before transplanting outdoors, harden off the seedlings for 1 to 2 weeks: gradually more hours outside and less protection.
respuestas.calendario: Frost limits many summer crops: tomato, basil, cucumber and squash are very sensitive. Find out the date of the last frost risk in your area (local agricultural services publish sowing calendars by region) and sow or transplant after it, or protect the plants with a cover.
respuestas.huerta: In the garden, compost and mulch help a lot: they improve soil structure and keep moisture. Rotate crop families year after year to reduce pests and diseases.
respuestas.riego: Before watering, check whether the soil or substrate is dry a few centimeters down. Over- and under-watering give similar symptoms, so it's worth logging every watering.
respuestas.luz: For LED light, intensity (PPFD), height and hours of light matter. Each stage has its range. Enter a measurement and the app tells you if it's outside the recommended range.
respuestas.masDatos: Tell me a bit more: what kind of plant it is, what stage it's in and what you see. Meanwhile, a tip: {{consejo}}

tips: Before watering, push a finger into the soil or substrate. If it's dry a few centimeters down, water.
Check the underside of the leaves: that's where most pests hide.
In inert substrates, water often with moderate volumes. They dry faster than soil.
Measure light at leaf height, not in the air.
Log every watering and every change. In a month you'll see patterns you can't see today.
In strong heat, water early so the plant has water before midday.
If a leaf changes color, also check the roots and watering before adding fertilizer.
tipsPorque: Roots need air as well as water. If you water while the substrate is still wet, the pores stay full of water, the roots suffocate and rot appears. In pots, overwatering is one of the most common causes of losing plants.

Aphids, spider mites, whiteflies and thrips shelter on the underside of leaves, away from the sun, and lay their eggs there. In warm weather their populations grow in a few days: spotting them while they're few lets you control them with gentle measures, like removing leaves or washing with water.
Perlite, coco coir and rockwool hold less water than soil and don't store nutrients. Small, frequent waterings keep moisture and the solution stable, and a little drainage prevents salt buildup.
Light intensity drops a lot as you move away from the lamp. If you measure higher or lower, the value isn't what the plant receives and you may correct the height in the wrong direction.
Symptoms often appear days after the cause. With entries you can link a change in watering, fertilizer or light to what happened later, and not repeat the mistake.

In the morning less water evaporates and the plant has it available for the hottest hours, when it transpires the most. Watering at midday wastes water to evaporation, and watering at night leaves leaves and soil wet longer, which favors fungi.
Overwatering or a damaged root prevents nutrient uptake and gives symptoms similar to a deficiency. Adding fertilizer in that case raises salts and makes the problem worse.

items: BROTA is an app to log your crops and learn about them. By using it you accept these terms.
The content is educational and general. It doesn't replace the advice of an agronomist or a specialist: for a serious problem, consult a professional.
The guide uses artificial intelligence and can make mistakes. Check its answers before applying any treatment.
BROTA doesn't give information about doses, consumption or sale of substances.
You're responsible for complying with the laws of your country regarding what you grow.
The Pro plan is paid through App Store or Google Play purchases. The subscription renews automatically until you cancel it from your store account, at least 24 hours before the period ends.
The Final exam certificate is an internal BROTA recognition, with no academic or legal validity.
You can delete your account and all your data whenever you want, from Settings > Profile.
We may update these terms. If the change is important, we'll let you know in the app.
